system.name: MotionStream
system.one_liner: A real-time autoregressive video diffusion model that streams long videos from one image with interactive motion-track control at 29.5 FPS and 0.39 s latency.

content.variant_note: two stacked lanes, an offline bidirectional model against the real-time autoregressive one, beside three application strips
content.argues: Prior motion-controlled video diffusion is offline, fixed-length and slow (0.79 FPS, 103 s latency); MotionStream streams infinite-length video in real time (29.5 FPS, 0.39 s) and serves interactive applications.
content.subject: Two lanes taking input tracks and one frame through a bidirectional versus an autoregressive diffusion model, and three strips: motion transfer, drag control, camera control.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw the prior method and the proposed one as two stacked lanes with the same icon recoloured and the same input, put speed numbers under each title, and make the difference visible (a fixed fan of frames against frames shrinking to an infinity sign); add capability strips for the applications.
lessons.suits: Teaser figures for systems whose selling point is speed or unbounded length and that serve several interactive applications.

evidence: Prior motion-controlled video diffusion models typically operate offline to generate fixed-length sequences in parallel (top left).
our MotionStream enables streaming long-video generation from a single image with track control at interactive speed

summary: MotionStream is a video diffusion model for interactive motion control that streams long videos in real time. Figure 1 is a teaser. Its left half stacks two lanes separated by a dashed rule: in the top lane fixed-length input tracks and an input frame enter a bidirectional model labelled G_teacher and give a fixed-length video at 0.79 FPS and 103 s latency; in the bottom lane streaming tracks and the same frame enter an autoregressive model labelled G_student and give an infinite stream of shrinking frames ending in an infinity sign at 29.5 FPS and 0.39 s latency, with the new words in red. The right half shows three photo strips: online motion transfer, drag-based control and camera control.
summary_zh: MotionStream是实时交互式运动控制视频生成模型。图1左半两条泳道对比离线双向模型（0.79 FPS、延迟103秒）与实时自回归模型（29.5 FPS、延迟0.39秒），右半三条图片带展示运动迁移、拖拽和相机控制。
notes: No paragraph of the paper text is available for this figure, so the teacher-student relation, the attention-grid meaning and the details of (a) are read from labels and from the abstract excerpt only; no distillation arrow is drawn. The two lanes are counted as panels because each has a bold title and a dashed rule between them. The orange and blue model colours are read off bitmaps and marked approximate.
